description:
A Denver, Colorado office park (lat=39.74, lon=-104.98) currently operates a 250 kW rooftop PV system and is evaluating adding battery storage to reduce utility demand charges. The client pays $22/kW-month on monthly peak 15-minute demand (~180 kW during business hours) plus $0.085/kWh for energy. Your firm has been hired to determine which battery size makes the best financial case.

Three battery configurations to evaluate:
  Config A: 100 kWh energy capacity / 50 kW power
  Config B: 200 kWh energy capacity / 100 kW power
  Config C: 400 kWh energy capacity / 100 kW power

Battery specifications (all configs):
- Lithium-ion (LFP), roundtrip efficiency: 92%
- Capacity fade: 2.5%/yr, lifetime: 15 years ($400/kWh replacement)
- Battery capex: $400/kWh installed
- Control strategy: peak shaving

PV system to co-simulate:
- 250 kW DC, tilt=20 deg, azimuth=180, DC/AC ratio=1.2, losses=14%
- Use real weather data for Denver, CO from SAM's solar resource library or NREL NSRDB
- Typical commercial building load: ~1,200,000 kWh/yr, peaking at ~180 kW on weekday business hours

Financial assumptions:
- Federal ITC: 30% (battery co-located with PV)
- Discount rate: 7.0%, analysis period: 25 years
- Energy escalation: 2.5%/yr

For each configuration, calculate: annual demand charge savings ($), annual energy savings ($), simple payback period (years), 25-year NPV ($), and 25-year IRR (%). Identify the optimal battery size by NPV.

Save results to: /home/ga/Documents/SAM_Projects/Denver_Commercial_Battery_Analysis.json

The JSON must contain a 'configurations' array (3 entries, each with: config_name, battery_kwh, battery_kw, annual_demand_charge_savings_usd, annual_energy_savings_usd, simple_payback_years, npv_25yr_usd, irr_pct), an 'optimal_configuration' field, a 'site' field ('Denver, CO'), and a 'recommendation_summary' field.
